tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages
tools.description: Read browser console messages (console.log, console.error, console.warn, etc.) from a specific tab. Useful for debugging JavaScript errors, viewing application logs, or understanding what's happening in the browser console. Returns console messages from the current domain only. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs. IMPORTANT: Always provide a pattern to filter messages - without a pattern, you may get too many irrelevant messages.

tabId.description: Tab ID to read console messages from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

onlyErrors.description: If true, only return error and exception messages. Default is false (return all message types).

clear.description: If true, clear the console messages after reading to avoid duplicates on subsequent calls. Default is false.

pattern.description: Regex pattern to filter console messages. Only messages matching this pattern will be returned (e.g., 'error|warning' to find errors and warnings, 'MyApp' to filter app-specific logs). You should always provide a pattern to avoid getting too many irrelevant messages.

limit.description: Maximum number of messages to return. Defaults to 100. Increase only if you need more results.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page
tools.description: Get an accessibility tree representation of elements on the page. By default returns all elements including non-visible ones. Output is limited to 50000 characters by default. If the output exceeds this limit it is truncated at a line boundary, with a note giving the full size — pass a larger max_chars, or use depth/ref_id to focus on part of the page. Optionally filter for only interactive elements. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.

filter.description: Filter elements: "interactive" for buttons/links/inputs only, "all" for all elements including non-visible ones (default: all elements)

tabId.description: Tab ID to read from. Must be a tab in the current group. Use tabs_context_mcp first if you don't have a valid tab ID.

depth.description: Maximum depth of the tree to traverse (default: 15). Use a smaller depth if output is too large.

ref_id.description: Reference ID of a parent element to read. Will return the specified element and all its children. Use this to focus on a specific part of the page when output is too large.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters for output (default: 50000). Set to a higher value if your client can handle large outputs.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp
tools.description: Close a tab in the MCP tab group by its ID. Use to clean up tabs you're done with. Only tabs in this session's group are closable; call tabs_context_mcp first to get valid IDs. If you close the group's last tab, Chrome auto-removes the group — the next tabs_context_mcp with createIfEmpty starts fresh.

tabId.description: The ID of the tab to close. Must be in this session's tab group. Get valid IDs from tabs_context_mcp.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp
tools.description: Get context information about the current MCP tab group. Returns all tab IDs inside the group if it exists. CRITICAL: You must get the context at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Each new conversation should create its own new tab (using tabs_create_mcp) rather than reusing existing tabs, unless the user explicitly asks to use an existing tab.

createIfEmpty.description: Creates a new MCP tab group if none exists, creates a new Window with a new tab group containing an empty tab (which can be used for this conversation). If a MCP tab group already exists, this parameter has no effect.

tools.name: DeferredToolPlaceholder
tools.description: Reserved placeholder that keeps deferred tool loading active; never call this tool.

tools.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
tools.description: Creates a new empty tab in the MCP tab group. CRITICAL: You must get the context using tabs_context_mcp at least once before using other browser automation tools so you know what tabs exist. Tabs you create are yours to clean up: close each one with tabs_close_mcp as soon as you no longer need it, and close any that remain before finishing your task. Leave a tab open only if the user asked to see it or wants it kept open.

input.content:
# Certificate Admin Console

An internal admin console for a multi-tenant training platform. Tenant admins can review certificates, bulk-issue them to eligible learners, revoke them, and export them to CSV.

- **Backend:** Python 3.11+, FastAPI, SQLite in WAL mode (`backend/`)
- **Frontend:** React 18, Vite, TypeScript (`frontend/`)
- **Agent instructions:** data model, rules and acceptance checks are in `AGENTS.md`

## Quick start

Requires Python ≥ 3.11 and Node ≥ 18.

```bash
./start.sh            # installs deps, seeds the demo data if the DB is empty, starts the API and UI
./start.sh --reset    # rebuilds the DB from the quick-start dataset first
./verify.sh           # runs acceptance tests A1–A7, then type-checks and builds the frontend
```

- UI: http://127.0.0.1:5173
- API: http://127.0.0.1:8000. Interactive docs are at `/docs`.

`verify.sh` starts each test with its own temporary database and its own server, so your dev database is never touched.

## Actors and tenants

There is no production authentication, by design. The actor is identified by request headers:

| Header | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `X-Actor` | Admin email, for example `alice@east.test` |
| `X-Tenant-Id` | Tenant to act in. Get the ids from `GET /api/me/tenants`. |

Admins and tenants are many-to-many through the `admin_tenants` table. Every tenant-scoped request is checked against that table:

- An unknown actor gets **401**.
- An admin who is not a member of the tenant gets **404**. The response does not reveal whether the tenant exists.

| Admin | Tenants | Tenant ids in a fresh DB |
|---|---|---|
| alice@east.test | East (Australia/Sydney) | 1 |
| bob@west.test | West (Australia/Perth) | 2 |
| carol@multi.test | East and West. Shows the many-to-many link and the tenant switcher in the UI. | 1, 2 |

In the UI, pick an admin, then pick one of that admin's tenants.

### Demo data, per tenant

- **Courses:** `Safety 101` and `First Aid 201`.
- **Safety 101 enrollments:**

| Learner | Enrollment | Certificate before any bulk issue |
|---|---|---|
| Alex Lee | completed | Already certified at `2026-01-10T13:30:00Z` |
| Sam Park | completed | None (eligible) |
| Taylor Wong | completed | None (eligible) |
| Jordan Kim | incomplete | None |

### Generating 100,000 rows

```bash
cd backend && .venv/bin/python -m app.gen_bulk --tenant East --count 100000
```

This adds a new course, `Load Test NNN`, with its own learners and certificates. It does not modify the quick-start rows; `./start.sh --reset` removes the generated data.

Names come from a pool of 100 and dates from 30 days, so many rows share the same sort-key value. Generation takes about 6 seconds.

## API

| Method | Path | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/actors` | Demo actor picker |
| GET | `/api/me/tenants` | Tenants of the current `X-Actor` |
| GET | `/api/courses` | Courses in the tenant |
| GET | `/api/certificates?q=&sort=&order=&page=&page_size=` | `sort` is one of `issued_date`, `learner_name`, `course_title`, `serial` |
| GET | `/api/certificates/export.csv?q=&sort=&order=` | Same filter and order as the list. Streamed. |
| GET | `/api/certificates/{id}` | Detail plus audit trail |
| POST | `/api/certificates/{id}/revoke` | Idempotent. The response includes `changed`. |
| POST | `/api/bulk-issues` | Body `{"course_id": N}`. Requires an `Idempotency-Key` header. |

## Acceptance scenarios

Each scenario has an automated test in `backend/tests/test_acceptance.py`. Run them all with `./verify.sh`, or one at a time:

```bash
cd backend && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v tests -k a2
```

- **Agent instructions:** data model, rules and acceptance checks are in `AGENTS.md`

## Quick start

Requires Python ≥ 3.11 and Node ≥ 18.

```bash
./start.sh            # installs deps, seeds the demo data if the DB is empty, starts the API and UI
./start.sh --reset    # rebuilds the DB from the quick-start dataset first
./verify.sh           # runs acceptance tests A1–A7, then type-checks and builds the frontend
```

- UI: http://127.0.0.1:5173
- API: http://127.0.0.1:8000. Interactive docs are at `/docs`.

`verify.sh` starts each test with its own temporary database and its own server, so your dev database is never touched.

## Actors and tenants

There is no production authentication, by design. The actor is identified by request headers:

| Header | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `X-Actor` | Admin email, for example `alice@east.test` |
| `X-Tenant-Id` | Tenant to act in. Get the ids from `GET /api/me/tenants`. |

Admins and tenants are many-to-many through the `admin_tenants` table. Every tenant-scoped request is checked against that table:

- An unknown actor gets **401**.
- An admin who is not a member of the tenant gets **404**. The response does not reveal whether the tenant exists.

| Admin | Tenants | Tenant ids in a fresh DB |
|---|---|---|
| alice@east.test | East (Australia/Sydney) | 1 |
| bob@west.test | West (Australia/Perth) | 2 |
| carol@multi.test | East and West. Shows the many-to-many link and the tenant switcher in the UI. | 1, 2 |

In the UI, pick an admin, then pick one of that admin's tenants.

### Demo data, per tenant

- **Courses:** `Safety 101` and `First Aid 201`.
- **Safety 101 enrollments:**

| Learner | Enrollment | Certificate before any bulk issue |
|---|---|---|
| Alex Lee | completed | Already certified at `2026-01-10T13:30:00Z` |
| Sam Park | completed | None (eligible) |
| Taylor Wong | completed | None (eligible) |
| Jordan Kim | incomplete | None |

### Generating 100,000 rows

```bash
cd backend && .venv/bin/python -m app.gen_bulk --tenant East --count 100000
```

This adds a new course, `Load Test NNN`, with its own learners and certificates. It does not modify the quick-start rows; `./start.sh --reset` removes the generated data.

Names come from a pool of 100 and dates from 30 days, so many rows share the same sort-key value. Generation takes about 6 seconds.

## API

| Method | Path | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/actors` | Demo actor picker |
| GET | `/api/me/tenants` | Tenants of the current `X-Actor` |
| GET | `/api/courses` | Courses in the tenant |
| GET | `/api/certificates?q=&sort=&order=&page=&page_size=` | `sort` is one of `issued_date`, `learner_name`, `course_title`, `serial` |
| GET | `/api/certificates/export.csv?q=&sort=&order=` | Same filter and order as the list. Streamed. |
| GET | `/api/certificates/{id}` | Detail plus audit trail |
| POST | `/api/certificates/{id}/revoke` | Idempotent. The response includes `changed`. |
| POST | `/api/bulk-issues` | Body `{"course_id": N}`. Requires an `Idempotency-Key` header. |

## Acceptance scenarios

Each scenario has an automated test in `backend/tests/test_acceptance.py`. Run them all with `./verify.sh`, or one at a time:

```bash
cd backend && .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v tests -k a2
```

For manual curl checks, start the app with `./start.sh --reset` and set `API=http://127.0.0.1:8000`.

### A1 — Tenant isolation (`test_a1_tenant_isolation`)

```bash
curl -i $API/api/certificates   -H 'X-Actor: bob@west.test' -H 'X-Tenant-Id: 1'   # 404
curl -i $API/api/certificates/1 -H 'X-Actor: bob@west.test' -H 'X-Tenant-Id: 2'   # 404 (cert 1 belongs to East)
curl -i -X POST $API/api/bulk-issues -H 'X-Actor: bob@west.test' -H 'X-Tenant-Id: 2' \
  -H 'Idempotency-Key: x' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"course_id":1}'  # 404
```

The test also covers revoke and export. It checks that no certificates, audit events or operations are created.

### A2 — Retry safety (`test_a2_retry_sequential_and_concurrent`)

The test sends 8 concurrent requests and then 2 sequential ones, all with the same key. All of them return the same `operation_id` and the same results. Only one response has `replayed: false`. The database then holds 2 new certificates and 2 ISSUE audit events.

To try it by hand, send this command several times, including in parallel:

```bash
curl -X POST $API/api/bulk-issues -H 'X-Actor: alice@east.test' -H 'X-Tenant-Id: 1' \
  -H 'Idempotency-Key: demo-1' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"course_id":1}'
```

### A3 — Key misuse (`test_a3_key_misuse_returns_409`)

Reuse the key `demo-1` with `{"course_id":2}`. The API returns **409**. No new rows are written, and replaying the original request still returns the original result.

### A4 — Learner outcomes (`test_a4_learner_outcomes`)

Bulk-issue East Safety 101. The result is:

| Learner | Outcome | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Alex Lee | skipped | `already_certified` |
| Jordan Kim | skipped | `incomplete` |
| Sam Park | issued | |
| Taylor Wong | issued | |

### A5 — DST and local date (`test_a5_tenant_local_dates`, `test_a5_sort_uses_local_date`)

Alex Lee's seeded certificate was issued at `2026-01-10T13:30:00Z`.

| Tenant | Displayed time | CSV date |
|---|---|---|
| East | `2026-01-11 00:30` | `2026-01-11` |
| West | `2026-01-10 21:30` | `2026-01-10` |

Sorting by issue date uses `issued_local_date`, then `issued_at`, then `id`.

### A6 — Export growth (`test_a6_export_100k`)

The test does the following:

1. Generates 100k East certificates.
2. Exports with `q=Lee&sort=learner_name&order=asc` twice. While the first export is streaming, it requests the list and checks that the list returns 200.
3. Checks both exports against an independent oracle: the matching rows sorted in Python by `(learner_name, id)`. Both exports must match it and match each other byte for byte.
4. Exports the full 100k dataset twice and checks the results are identical.

Measured: the full 100k export takes about 0.6 seconds.

### A7 — Revocation audit (`test_a7_revocation_audit`)

- The first revoke returns `changed: true` and writes one REVOKE audit event.
- A second revoke, and 4 more concurrent repeats, return `changed: false` and write no audit events.

## Key design decisions

- **Idempotency:** The whole bulk operation runs in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction: claiming the key, issuing certificates, writing audit events and storing the result. SQLite allows only one writer at a time, so concurrent requests with the same key queue up. Each one then reads the committed result. If the operation crashes, everything rolls back, so a half-finished operation is never visible. A key reused with a different `request_hash` gets 409. Keys are scoped per tenant.
- **No duplicates, enforced in the database:**
  - `UNIQUE(tenant_id, learner_id, course_id)` on certificates.
  - `UNIQUE(certificate_id, action)` on audit events.
  - Revoke is a conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE status='ACTIVE'`, and the audit event is written only when exactly one row changed.
- **Stable ordering:** Every sort ends with `id`. The list and the CSV export use the same query builder (`backend/app/certs.py`).
- **Export:** Streamed in batches of 5,000 rows from a single read transaction, so the file is a consistent snapshot. In WAL mode a reader does not block list requests or writers.
- **Local date:** `issued_local_date` is computed once, at issue time, from the tenant's timezone. Displayed times are converted from `issued_at` UTC on each request.
- **Revoked certificates are not re-issued.** They are skipped as `already_certified`.

## Known limitations and unfinished work

- **SQLite single writer.** A bulk issue holds the write lock for its whole duration. Concurrent writes, such as a revoke, wait up to 30 seconds via `busy_timeout`. That is fine at demo scale; on PostgreSQL I would claim the key with a row lock and process learners in batches.
- **Same-key callers wait synchronously.** A concurrent caller blocks until the first operation commits. There is no "202 + poll" flow.
- **Idempotency keys never expire.**
- **The list uses OFFSET pagination.** Very deep pages on 100k rows get slower. Export is not affected.
- **Contains-search scans the tenant's rows.** `LIKE '%q%'` cannot use an index. It is fast enough at 100k; a full-text index would be needed beyond that.
- **Serial collisions are not retried.** Serials are 10 random hex characters. A collision is reported as a `failed` outcome for that learner rather than retried.
- **UI export buffers the file in memory.** The UI downloads the CSV via `fetch` into a blob, about 5 MB at 100k rows, so that it can send the actor headers. The API itself streams.
- **No UI tests.** The UI was checked manually: actor and tenant switching, bulk issue, list, detail, revoke confirmation, and audit trail.
- **Running `gen_bulk` twice adds another 100k rows** under a new course.

COURSE_SUMMARY_SQL = """
SELECT c.id, c.title,
       COUNT(e.id)                                                AS enrolled,
       COALESCE(SUM(e.status = 'COMPLETED'), 0)                   AS completed,
       COALESCE(SUM(e.status = 'INCOMPLETE'), 0)                  AS incomplete,
       COALESCE(SUM(ct.status = 'ACTIVE'), 0)                     AS certified_active,
       COALESCE(SUM(ct.status = 'REVOKED'), 0)                    AS certified_revoked,
       COALESCE(SUM(e.status = 'COMPLETED' AND ct.id IS NULL), 0) AS eligible
FROM courses c
LEFT JOIN enrollments e  ON e.course_id = c.id AND e.tenant_id = c.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN certificates ct ON ct.tenant_id = e.tenant_id AND ct.learner_id = e.learner_id
                         AND ct.course_id = e.course_id
WHERE c.tenant_id = ? {extra}
GROUP BY c.id
ORDER BY c.title, c.id
"""


@app.get("/api/courses")
def list_courses(ctx: TenantCtx = Depends(get_tenant_ctx), conn: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(get_conn)):
    rows = conn.execute(COURSE_SUMMARY_SQL.format(extra=""), (ctx.tenant_id,)).fetchall()
    return [dict(r) for r in rows]


@app.get("/api/courses/{course_id}")
def get_course(course_id: int, ctx: TenantCtx = Depends(get_tenant_ctx),
               conn: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(get_conn)):
    row = conn.execute(COURSE_SUMMARY_SQL.format(extra="AND c.id = ?"), (ctx.tenant_id, course_id)).fetchone()
    if not row:
        raise HTTPException(404, "course not found")
    return dict(row)


@app.get("/api/courses/{course_id}/enrollments")
def list_enrollments(
    course_id: int,
    page: int = Query(1, ge=1),
    page_size: int = Query(20, ge=1, le=100),
    ctx: TenantCtx = Depends(get_tenant_ctx),
    conn: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(get_conn),
):
    if not conn.execute("SELECT 1 FROM courses WHERE id = ? AND tenant_id = ?", (course_id, ctx.tenant_id)).fetchone():
        raise HTTPException(404, "course not found")
    total = conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM enrollments WHERE tenant_id = ? AND course_id = ?",
                         (ctx.tenant_id, course_id)).fetchone()[0]
    rows = conn.execute(
        "SELECT e.id, e.learner_id, l.name AS learner_name, e.status, e.completed_at,"
        "       ct.id AS certificate_id, ct.serial, ct.status AS certificate_status"
        " FROM enrollments e"
        " JOIN learners l ON l.id = e.learner_id AND l.tenant_id = e.tenant_id"
        " LEFT JOIN certificates ct ON ct.tenant_id = e.tenant_id AND ct.learner_id = e.learner_id"
        "      AND ct.course_id = e.course_id"
        " WHERE e.tenant_id = ? AND e.course_id = ?"
        " ORDER BY l.name, e.id LIMIT ? OFFSET ?",
        (ctx.tenant_id, course_id, page_size, (page - 1) * page_size),
    ).fetchall()
    items = [{**dict(r),
              "completed_local": local_datetime(r["completed_at"], ctx.timezone) if r["completed_at"] else None}
             for r in rows]
    return {"items": items, "total": total, "page": page, "page_size": page_size}

COURSE_SUMMARY_SQL = """
SELECT c.id, c.title,
       COUNT(e.id)                                                AS enrolled,
       COALESCE(SUM(e.status = 'COMPLETED'), 0)                   AS completed,
       COALESCE(SUM(e.status = 'INCOMPLETE'), 0)                  AS incomplete,
       COALESCE(SUM(ct.status = 'ACTIVE'), 0)                     AS certified_active,
       COALESCE(SUM(ct.status = 'REVOKED'), 0)                    AS certified_revoked,
       COALESCE(SUM(e.status = 'COMPLETED' AND ct.id IS NULL), 0) AS eligible
FROM courses c
LEFT JOIN enrollments e  ON e.course_id = c.id AND e.tenant_id = c.tenant_id
LEFT JOIN certificates ct ON ct.tenant_id = e.tenant_id AND ct.learner_id = e.learner_id
                         AND ct.course_id = e.course_id
WHERE c.tenant_id = ? {extra}
GROUP BY c.id
ORDER BY c.title, c.id
"""


@app.get("/api/courses")
def list_courses(ctx: TenantCtx = Depends(get_tenant_ctx), conn: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(get_conn)):
    rows = conn.execute(COURSE_SUMMARY_SQL.format(extra=""), (ctx.tenant_id,)).fetchall()
    return [dict(r) for r in rows]


@app.get("/api/courses/{course_id}")
def get_course(course_id: int, ctx: TenantCtx = Depends(get_tenant_ctx),
               conn: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(get_conn)):
    row = conn.execute(COURSE_SUMMARY_SQL.format(extra="AND c.id = ?"), (ctx.tenant_id, course_id)).fetchone()
    if not row:
        raise HTTPException(404, "course not found")
    return dict(row)


@app.get("/api/courses/{course_id}/enrollments")
def list_enrollments(
    course_id: int,
    page: int = Query(1, ge=1),
    page_size: int = Query(20, ge=1, le=100),
    ctx: TenantCtx = Depends(get_tenant_ctx),
    conn: sqlite3.Connection = Depends(get_conn),
):
    if not conn.execute("SELECT 1 FROM courses WHERE id = ? AND tenant_id = ?", (course_id, ctx.tenant_id)).fetchone():
        raise HTTPException(404, "course not found")
    total = conn.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM enrollments WHERE tenant_id = ? AND course_id = ?",
                         (ctx.tenant_id, course_id)).fetchone()[0]
    rows = conn.execute(
        "SELECT e.id, e.learner_id, l.name AS learner_name, e.status, e.completed_at,"
        "       ct.id AS certificate_id, ct.serial, ct.status AS certificate_status"
        " FROM enrollments e"
        " JOIN learners l ON l.id = e.learner_id AND l.tenant_id = e.tenant_id"
        " LEFT JOIN certificates ct ON ct.tenant_id = e.tenant_id AND ct.learner_id = e.learner_id"
        "      AND ct.course_id = e.course_id"
        " WHERE e.tenant_id = ? AND e.course_id = ?"
        " ORDER BY l.name, e.id LIMIT ? OFFSET ?",
        (ctx.tenant_id, course_id, page_size, (page - 1) * page_size),
    ).fetchall()
    items = [{**dict(r),
              "completed_local": local_datetime(r["completed_at"], ctx.timezone) if r["completed_at"] else None}
             for r in rows]
    return {"items": items, "total": total, "page": page, "page_size": page_size}

课程列表和课程详情已经做好并提交了（`f406f1c`）。`./verify.sh` 跑下来 10 个测试全过，前端也能正常构建。我在浏览器里点了一遍，流程是通的。

**新增内容**
- **课程列表**（默认打开的页签）：列出当前租户的所有课程，每门课显示报名、已完成、未完成、已发证（含已吊销）和可发证的人数。
- **课程详情**：顶部是统计数字；中间是批量发证面板，课程已选好；下面是报名表，列出学员、报名状态、完成时间（租户本地时间）和证书。证书序列号可以点开，查看证书详情或吊销。
- **批量发证的位置**：从原来的独立面板移到了课程详情页里，发证后统计数字和报名表会自动刷新。
- **接口**：新增 `GET /api/courses/{id}` 和 `/api/courses/{id}/enrollments`，后者分页，因为生成的测试课程有 10 万个报名。跨租户访问返回 404，这一点有新测试覆盖。

**顺带修了两个真实的问题，都可以写进 decision-log**
1. **测试残留进程**：之前那次因代理配置失败的测试运行，留下了 9 个没有关掉的 uvicorn 进程。原因是测试在等待后端启动时，遇到的异常不是 `HTTPError`，就跳过了关闭后端进程的那一步。现在改成无论成功失败都会关闭。
2. **`start.sh` 会悄悄连上旧后端**：本次验证时，8000 端口被旧进程占着，新后端启动失败，但前端照样起来了，页面连的是旧代码。现在端口被占或后端没启动成功，脚本会直接报错退出。

README 和 `AGENTS.md` 都已同步更新。还没做的仍是那三项需要你自己处理的交付物：`ai/` 下的会话导出和索引、`decision-log.md`、`written-answers.md`。

content.text:
下面按场景说明实现方式，并给出对应的代码位置。路径都相对仓库根目录，测试都在 `backend/tests/test_acceptance.py`。

## 前提：租户上下文怎么确定
后续每个场景都依赖这一层，建议先看这里。
- 每个和租户相关的接口都通过 `Depends(get_tenant_ctx)` 拿到上下文，实现在 `backend/app/deps.py:43`。
- 它会把 `X-Actor` 和 `X-Tenant-Id` 两个请求头与 `admin_tenants` 表做 JOIN 校验（`deps.py:53`）。不是该租户的成员就返回 404（`deps.py:58`）；actor 不存在则返回 401（`deps.py:36-39`）。
- 后面所有 SQL 用的 `tenant_id` 都取自校验后的 `ctx.tenant_id`，不会直接读请求参数。

## A1 租户隔离
- **Bob 声称自己属于 East**：`get_tenant_ctx` 这一层就返回 404，列表、详情、吊销、导出、批量发证都到不了业务代码。
- **Bob 在 West 租户下传 East 的资源 ID**：查询都带了 `AND tenant_id = ?`，查不到就返回 404。
  - 证书详情和吊销：`main.py:176-179`
  - 批量发证里查课程：`bulk.py:42-46`
  - 课程相关接口：`main.py:81`、`main.py:93`
  - 列表和导出共用的 WHERE 条件：`certs.py:27`
- **跨租户的批量发证不会留下任何数据**：查课程这一步在写事务里面，返回 404 时事务回滚（`db.py:28-35` 会捕获异常并执行 ROLLBACK）。所以不会产生 operation、证书或审计记录。
- 测试：`test_a1_tenant_isolation`（第 76 行），断言请求前后各表的行数没有变化。

## A2 重试安全
- **整个操作放在一个事务里**：抢占幂等 key、发证、写审计、保存结果，全部在一个 `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` 写事务中完成（`bulk.py:31` 的 `with write_tx` 到 `bulk.py:104`）。
- **并发请求会排队**：SQLite 同一时刻只允许一个写事务，用同一个 key 并发进来的第二个请求会在 BEGIN 处等待（`db.py:23` 设置了 `busy_timeout=30s`）。等它拿到锁时，前一个已经提交，它会查到那条 operation，原样返回保存的 `result_json`，并带上 `replayed: true`（`bulk.py:32-40`）。
- **数据库层的兜底**（`backend/app/schema.sql`）：
  - `UNIQUE(tenant_id, idempotency_key)`（第 72 行）
  - 证书 `UNIQUE(tenant_id, learner_id, course_id)`（第 56 行）
  - 审计 `UNIQUE(certificate_id, action)`（第 83 行）
- **发证和审计成对写入**：两条 INSERT 在同一个 SAVEPOINT 里（`bulk.py:77-96`），要么都写入，要么都不写。
- **前端**：用 `inFlight` ref 防止重复点击，请求进行中按钮禁用（`App.tsx:340`、`App.tsx:361`）。失败重试时沿用同一个 key，成功后才换新 key（`App.tsx:335-347`）。
- 测试：`test_a2_retry_sequential_and_concurrent`（第 106 行）。先发 8 个并发请求，再发 2 个顺序请求，断言 `operation_id` 只有一个、结果完全一致、`replayed=false` 只出现一次，并检查证书数和审计数。

## A3 幂等 key 被挪用
- `request_hash` 是对 `{"course_id": ...}` 计算的 sha256（`bulk.py:22-23`）。key 已存在但 hash 不同时返回 409（`bulk.py:39`），事务回滚，不执行任何操作，也不覆盖原来的结果。
- key 的检查在课程校验**之前**，所以就算换成一个不存在的课程，返回的也是 409。
- 测试：`test_a3_key_misuse_returns_409`（第 136 行），还会验证用原请求重放时拿到的仍是第一次的结果。

## A4 每个学员的处理结果
- 遍历该课程的所有报名记录（`bulk.py:56-66`）：
  - 未完成课程 → `skipped: incomplete`（`bulk.py:70`）
  - 已有证书（包括已吊销的）→ `skipped: already_certified`（`bulk.py:73`）
  - 其余正常发证
  - 单个学员插入时发生数据库异常 → `ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT`，记为 `failed`，不影响其他学员（`bulk.py:94`）
- 测试：`test_a4_learner_outcomes`（第 155 行）。

## A5 夏令时与本地日期
- `issued_at` 以 UTC 存储。发证时用租户时区（`zoneinfo`，会自动处理夏令时）算出 `issued_local_date` 并一起存下（`db.py:51`，写入位置在 `bulk.py:81`）。
- 页面显示时由 `local_datetime` 实时换算（`db.py:55`，在 `main.py:24` 调用）。1 月份悉尼是夏令时 UTC+11，所以显示 `2026-01-11 00:30`；珀斯是 UTC+8，显示 `2026-01-10 21:30`。
- 按日期排序用的是 `issued_local_date, issued_at, id`（`certs.py:6`）。CSV 导出的也是 `issued_local_date`（`main.py:144`）。
- 测试：`test_a5_tenant_local_dates`（第 170 行）和 `test_a5_sort_uses_local_date`（第 185 行）。
- 有一个限制：本地日期是在发证时就算好存下的，如果之后修改租户的时区，已有证书的日期不会跟着变。我按"租户时区不可修改"处理了。

## A6 10 万行导出
- **列表和导出共用一套查询**：都调用 `build_query`（`certs.py:22`），所以筛选和排序条件完全一致（`main.py:126` 和 `main.py:143`）。
- **顺序稳定**：所有排序都以 `id` 作为最后的排序键（`certs.py:5-10`、`certs.py:35`），排序值相同的行每次导出的相对顺序也一样。
- **流式输出**：导出用独立的数据库连接，在一个读事务里分批 `fetchmany(5000)`，边查边写给客户端（`main.py:147-166`）。整份文件来自同一个快照。
- **导出时不阻塞列表**：数据库开了 WAL 模式（`db.py:21`），读不阻塞写，长时间的导出也不会挡住列表请求。接口是同步函数，FastAPI 会把它放到线程池里执行。
- **10 万行数据**：由 `backend/app/gen_bulk.py` 生成。学员名从 100 个里选、日期在 30 天内分布，所以排序值相同的行很多。
- 测试：`test_a6_export_100k`（第 196 行）。
  - 用 Python 独立算出期望结果（按 `(learner_name, id)` 排序），和导出结果对比。
  - 连续导出两次，要求内容逐字节一致。
  - 第一次导出还在传输时请求列表，要求返回 200。
  - 还要求每次导出在 60 秒内完成，全量导出两次也要一致。实测全量导出约 0.6 秒。

## A7 吊销的审计
- 吊销用一条带条件的 UPDATE：`... WHERE id=? AND tenant_id=? AND status='ACTIVE'`（`main.py:196-211`）。只有影响了 1 行（`main.py:205`）才写 REVOKE 审计，而且和 UPDATE 在同一个写事务里。
- 重复吊销时影响行数为 0，返回 `changed: false`，不写审计。`UNIQUE(certificate_id, action)` 在数据库层兜底。
- **前端**：吊销需要页面内的二次确认（`App.tsx:658` 一带）。
- 测试：`test_a7_revocation_audit`（第 242 行）。包括先后两次吊销和 4 个并发吊销，断言 REVOKE 审计只有 1 条。

## 建议重点核对的地方
1. `bulk.py:31-104`：整个事务的边界，以及 HTTPException 抛出时是否真的会回滚（看 `db.py:31-35`）。
2. `certs.py`：排序的最后一列是不是始终是 `id`，desc 时 `id` 也跟着 desc。
3. `main.py:147-166`：导出的生成器里自己开连接和关连接。这里不能复用 `Depends(get_conn)`，因为流式响应还在输出时，依赖可能已经被清理掉了。

# Decision Log

## D1 — Corrected: admins ↔ tenants changed from one-to-many to many-to-many, with a membership check on every request

**Type:** AI suggestion rejected / corrected

**What the AI proposed.** The first data model (planning turn, before any code) put `tenant_id` directly on the `admins` table, so each admin belonged to exactly one tenant.

**What I changed and why.** In a multi-tenant SaaS product, one admin often manages several tenants, and one tenant has several admins. Modelling that as one-to-many would have to be migrated later. I asked for three things:

- A join table, `admin_tenants`.
- A tenant list endpoint and a tenant switcher in the UI.
- A backend check, on every request, that the actor really belongs to the requested tenant. The client's word is not trusted.

All other resources stay isolated per tenant. I also asked for a demo admin who belongs to both tenants, `carol@multi.test`. The brief's required accounts are unchanged: `alice@east.test` belongs to East only and `bob@west.test` to West only.

**Result.**

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Join table | `backend/app/schema.sql`, `admin_tenants` |
| Membership check, returns 404 to non-members | `backend/app/deps.py`, `get_tenant_ctx` |
| Tenant list endpoint | `GET /api/me/tenants` |
| Tenant switcher, remounts all tenant-scoped state on switch | `frontend/src/App.tsx` |

**Verification.**

- `test_actor_context_and_membership`: carol sees both tenants and bob sees only West. An unknown actor gets 401.
- `test_a1_tenant_isolation`: bob gets 404 on East through the list, detail, revoke, export and bulk-issue endpoints. Row counts are unchanged afterwards.
- Manual UI check: as carol, switched between East and West.

**Commits.** `2e4fcc5` (model in AGENTS.md), `2568457` (implementation), `3735bb1` (tests)

---

## D2 — Accepted: run the whole bulk-issue operation in one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction for idempotency

**Type:** AI suggestion accepted

**Proposal.** One SQLite write transaction covers the whole operation:

1. Claim the idempotency key (look it up; insert it if absent).
2. Issue certificates and write their audit events.
3. Store the result as `result_json`.

SQLite allows only one writer at a time. A concurrent request with the same key therefore waits on the lock, then reads the committed result and replays it. A crash rolls back everything, so a half-done operation is never visible. A key reused with a different payload returns 409.

**Alternative considered.** Insert a `RUNNING` row first, then have concurrent callers poll it. This needs extra handling for operations that crash halfway and leave a stuck `RUNNING` row. With SQLite it adds complexity and no benefit.

**Why I accepted.**

- Correctness does not depend on application-level locking.
- Database constraints act as a backstop: `UNIQUE(tenant_id, idempotency_key)`, `UNIQUE(tenant_id, learner_id, course_id)` on certificates, and `UNIQUE(certificate_id, action)` on audit events.
- It is simple enough to review within the time limit.

**Trade-off I accepted knowingly.** A bulk issue holds the write lock for its whole duration. Concurrent callers block, waiting up to `busy_timeout` = 30 s, instead of receiving a 202 and polling. The README lists this under known limitations, together with how I would change it on PostgreSQL (row-lock claim, batched processing).

**Verification.**

- `test_a2_retry_sequential_and_concurrent`: 8 concurrent plus 2 sequential requests with one key give one `operation_id` and identical results. Only one response has `replayed=false`. The database holds 2 new certificates and 2 ISSUE audit events.
- `test_a3_key_misuse_returns_409`: reusing a key with a different payload returns 409. No rows are written, and replaying the original request still returns the original result.
- I reviewed `bulk.py` against `db.write_tx` to confirm that `HTTPException` (404 / 409) triggers a ROLLBACK.

**Commits.** `2568457`, `3735bb1`

---

## D3 — Scope: add a read-only course list and course detail, scoped to the current tenant

**Type:** Scope / design trade-off

**Context.** The required scope (brief §3) lists certificate list, bulk issue, certificate detail and CSV export. The product description, however, starts with "Tenant admins **review course completions**". Without a course view, an admin issues certificates blind: they cannot see who has completed a course, who is incomplete, or who is already certified.

**Decision.** I proposed adding a course list and a course detail page showing enrollments. The AI agreed, but recommended keeping it narrow. I accepted these limits:

- **Read-only.** No create, edit or delete for courses or enrollments. The brief says not to add unrelated features.
- **Current tenant only.** The course list is not aggregated across an admin's tenants, so the A1 isolation model is unchanged.
- **Bulk issue moves into the course detail page,** so the admin sees eligibility before issuing.
- **Enrollments are paginated,** because the load-test course has 100k enrollments.

**Verification.**

- `test_course_summary_and_enrollments`: counts are correct before and after a bulk issue, and the new endpoints return 404 across tenants.
- Manual UI pass: course list → Safety 101 → bulk issue. The counts refreshed (Certified 3, Eligible 0) and the enrollment rows showed the new serials.

**Commit.** `f406f1c`

---

## D4 — Defects in AI-written code, caught by verification

**Type:** AI output corrected

These are real defects that appeared in this session, each caught by running something. None is invented for this log.

### 1. Test fixture leaked server processes

**How it was found.** While verifying D3 in the browser, the API returned the old `/api/courses` response without the new count fields.

**Root causes.**

- **Leaked servers.** An earlier test run had failed because of the environment's SOCKS proxy. The pytest fixture only caught `httpx.HTTPError` while waiting for the server to start, so the `ImportError` escaped and 9 uvicorn subprocesses were never terminated.
- **Stale backend.** The API launched by an earlier `start.sh` run was still listening on port 8000, so the new backend failed to bind (the log showed `address already in use`). `start.sh` carried on and started Vite anyway, so the UI silently talked to the old backend.

**Fix.**

- The fixture now uses `try/finally` and always terminates the server, killing it if needed.
- `start.sh` fails fast if port 8000 or 5173 is taken, or if the API does not become healthy.

**Verification.** After `./verify.sh`, `ps aux | grep uvicorn` shows 0 processes. A second `./start.sh` exits with "Port 8000 is already in use".

**Commit.** `f406f1c`

### 2. Tests could not reach the local server

**Symptom.** The first test run errored with `Using SOCKS proxy, but the 'socksio' package is not installed`.

**Cause.** The environment's proxy settings were applied to localhost calls.

**Fix.** `trust_env=False` on the test HTTP clients.

**Commit.** `3735bb1`

### 3. Unstable React context object

**Problem.** In `App`, `ctx` was rebuilt on every render. Every effect that depends on `ctx` (courses, certificate list) would have refetched on unrelated re-renders.

**How it was found.** Caught when reviewing the component after the first build.

**Fix.** Memoised it with `useMemo`.

**Commit.** `8244203`

---

## Other recorded choices (minor)

| Choice | Reason | Where |
|---|---|---|
| SQLite in WAL mode, not PostgreSQL | One-command startup with no Docker. WAL lets the export read while writes continue. | `db.py` |
| Revoked certificates are not re-issued (`already_certified`) | Keeps one certificate row per learner and course; confirmed with the AI during planning. | `bulk.py` |
| Idempotency keys scoped per tenant | Confirmed during planning | `schema.sql` |
| `issued_local_date` stored at issue time | Index-friendly sort and export. Assumes a tenant's timezone never changes; this assumption is documented. | `db.local_date` |
| Every sort ends with `id`; list and export share one query builder | Deterministic ordering for A6 | `certs.py` |
